title: Session Spinup Heuristic Playbook
content:
Purpose:
- Quick personal playbook for heuristics used when creating / resuming ephemeral user sessions. Balance cost (warm GPUs) vs latency (cold starts) for interactive flows.

Background / motivation (short):
- Many client interactions require near-instant response (chat UI).
- Full warmup of model runtime (loading weights, kv cache priming, prefetching embeddings) is expensive.
- We can cheat with light-weight partial warmups and heuristics to reduce median latency while keeping cost acceptable.
- This doc collects ideas and an API/config sketch to experiment with in sandbox.

High level goals:
- Reduce P95 latency for first interactive token without keeping GPUs idling for long periods.
- Provide deterministic behavior for critical flows (payments, auth flows) where latency matters.
- Expose simple knobs for product teams: aggressive, opportunistic, conservative.

Constraints / assumptions:
- Runtime exposes a "fast-attach" path to resume a session container with minimal cold-start (~100-400ms optimistic).
- We have prefix/KV caching support but no cheap snapshot restore yet (that’s future).
- User sessions have affinity metadata (tenant id, device hint, last-active timestamp).
- Telemetry available: last_request_ts, median_latency_1h, request_rate_5m, token_dist_mean.

API surface (sketch) - HTTP endpoints the client or edge-proxy can call:
- POST /v1/session/probe { client_id, user_id, signal_set } -> 200/202 + hints
  - Purpose: lightweight probe (no token generation) to request a warmup decision and lease.
- POST /v1/session/warmup { session_template, warmup_level } -> 202 accepted
  - session_template: model, max_seq_len, context_seed (optional), tools_enabled[]
  - warmup_level: none | prefetch | kv-primed | full-load
- GET /v1/session/status/{lease_id} -> returns state and estimated-ready-in
- POST /v1/session/cancel/{lease_id} -> revoke warmup lease

Example responses (text-only sketch):
- probe -> { decision: \"opt-in\" | \"defer\", suggested_level: \"kv-primed\", lease_ttl: 30s, cost_estimate_tokens: 40 }
- warmup accepted -> { lease_id: L-xxxx, started_at, expected_ready_ms }

Config schema (runtime heuristics) - YAML-esque, for per-route profiles:
- spinup_profiles:
    - name: conservative
      max_budget_ms: 120000  # how long to keep warm before letting go
      min_request_rate_per_min: 10  # keep if traffic above
      preference: keep-kv-longer
    - name: opportunistic
      max_budget_ms: 30000
      min_request_rate_per_min: 2
      prefetch_on_probe: true
    - name: aggressive
      max_budget_ms: 10000
      min_request_rate_per_min: 0
      prefetch_on_probe: false

Runtime decision logic (notes-to-self):
- Inputs: recent request rate (5m/1h), last_active delta, client_hint (foreground/background), route_priority, account_tier (free vs paid), estimated-cost-per-minute
- Simple scoring: score = a*rate + b*(1 - idle_fraction) + c*tier_bonus - d*cost; threshold -> spinup
- If a probe arrives and score borderline -> suggest `kv-primed` and short lease (e.g., 15s). If strict SLO route -> force `full-load`.

Lifecycle diagrams (ASCII):
- client flow (fastpath)
  Client UI -> edge-proxy -> POST /probe -> decision: opt-in -> POST /warmup -> lease-> runtime warms -> GET /status -> ready -> client sends first generate request -> attach lease -> runtime increments usage

  [Client]--probe-->[Edge]--probe-->[SpinupSvc]--->(decision)-->[Runtime]
  (lease TTL 15s)

- resource reclamation: lease expires -> graceful-evict (save minimal metadata) -> release GPU slot

Tradeoffs & heuristics notes:
- Prefetching embeddings for the last N messages is cheap vs full kv priming. Try to bias toward embedding prefetch for multi-tool flows.
- Use short leases for mobile foreground events (e.g., app opened) because user often interacts within 10s. Desktop web sessions can have longer leases.
- For high-value accounts, allow longer `max_budget_ms` and fast fallback paths.

Experiments to run (quick list):
- A/B: opportunistic vs conservative profiles for chat median latency and GPU-hours consumed per 1k users.
- Probe TTL sweep: 5s, 15s, 30s — measure attach success and wasted warmups.
- Prefetch-only vs KV-primed: instrument token cost delta and P95 latency.

Implementation TODOs (personal):
- [ ] wire minimal probe endpoint on ingress adapter (Riley) - rough impl in infra pr 1234
- [ ] runtime: expose `lease` resource with TTL + metric hooks (Marco)
- [ ] add per-route profile UI in console: dropdown choose profile id
- [ ] add telemetry events: probe.sent, warmup.started, warmup.ready, warmup.evicted
- [ ] build lightweight simulator to approximate cost/latency tradeoffs (python notebook)

Open questions / unresolved decisions:
- How aggressive can we be w.r.t. KV priming memory use? Need concrete mem budget per tenant.
- Should a probe be rate-limited per device to avoid warmup storms when app is backgrounding multiple tabs? (likely yes)
- Do we allow clients to opt-out globally (privacy)? Add `allow_probe: bool` in client config.
- What are billing implications? Warmup token estimate vs actual usage — need finance input before we surface to customers.

Notes to self (quick heuristics):
- If last_active < 30s and rate_5m > 1 -> likely to accept lease
- Foreground flag + high-priority route -> bump suggested_level by one step
- If multiple probes for same user within 5s -> consolidate into single warmup and extend lease slightly

Saved sketches / commands:
- curl -X POST https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/session/probe -d '{"client_id":"web-foo","user_id":"u-123","signal_set":{"foreground":true}}'
- sample decision logic pseudo: score = 2*rate5m + 1*(foreground?1:0) + tierBonus - 0.5*(idleMinutes)

References / related artifacts (for later clean copy):
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1234 (temp spinup API)
- perf sim notebook: /notebooks/spinup-sim.ipynb (local)
- JIRA: INF-987 (ephemeral session lifecycle)

Final: this is a messy running doc. Keep experimental flags behind feature gate. Next step: prototype probe endpoint + simple TTL lease using existing lease-manager in infra branch.

-- Evelyn
